Frontier College is a national literacy organization, established in 1899 on the belief that literacy is a right. We work collaboratively with almost 500 community-based agencies across Canada to provide targeted literacy, numeracy, and essential skills support for Canadians.     Our experience over 120 years has demonstrated that, when delivered through existing community hubs and networks, literacy and essential skills interventions are high impact, low cost, and can be adapted to diverse geographies, local economies, and demographics of participants. Research demonstrates that literacy is intricately connected to multiple other societal issues including poverty, employment, civic engagement, criminal justice, health care, and others.    Our public policy efforts seek to focus government attention on the critical importance of literacy and its relationship to these other societal issues. Specifically, our hope is that the government will: create a National Literacy Secretariat to align the efforts of the provinces and the federal Office of Literacy and Essential Skills (Employment and Social Development Canada); and, more recently, to invest in workplace literacy and essential skills programs as part of its response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

MADD Canada identifies policies, laws and administrative sanctions that will reduce the number of Canadians being killed and injured in impaired driving crashes every year. MADD Canada promotes these policies to elected officials and decision makers at both the Federal and Provincial/Territorial levels.       At the Federal level, MADD Canada communicated with elected officials to promote the need for: improved testing measures for drug-impaired drivers, particularly since the legalization of cannabis; mandatory alcohol screening; and improved sentencing for the most serious impaired driving offences. These strategies are laid out in our Top Ten Report for the Federal Government. This report is based on best practices in Canada and throughout other democratic countries. The focus of the report is to enable the Federal Government to reduce impaired driving deaths and injuries. This report is available on our website.       At the Provincial/Territorial level, MADD Canada communicated with leaders and decision makers in various jurisdictions to promote the need for: .00% BAC restrictions for young drivers until age 21; immediate roadside licence suspensions and vehicle impoundments for drivers in the .05% to .08% BAC range; mandatory alcohol interlocks for drivers convicted of impaired driving offences; administrative sanctions for drug-impaired drivers; and other measures to reduce and prevent impaired driving. These strategies are laid out in our Top Ten Report for Provinces and Territories. Every Province and Territory has individual recommendations to reduce impaired deaths and injuries. This report is available on our website.

MLSS conducts research to identify and compile science-based evidence of the ecological values and services provided by marine ecosystems, such as the unique glass sponge reefs in British Columbia, that in the long term are important components of food-web resources for the public. MLSS communications with these agencies are directed at providing evidence that support policies such as the DFO Fisheries policies and frameworks on conservation and sustainability.  Similarly, MLSS disseminates this information to the public through presentations, in person (when feasible) or virtually to raise awareness of the importance of protecting ecosystems as the habitats that support the resources that we consume.   Dissemination of this information is intended to educate the public about the need to protect diversity of marine life for the sake of sustainability as well as informing the public of the interconnectedness of our actions in protecting the diversity of ecosystems and the ramifications of such actions if we don't.  MLSS advocates with government agencies to ensure that the policies, laws, regulations and protection established specifically to protect marine life are strictly adhered to, followed and enforced.    MLSS has provided and corresponded with DFO Scientific Researchers regarding original sponge reef data that was evidence to support the protection of glass sponge reefs as Marine Refuges under the precautionary approach process.  MLSS communicated these results with the public through scientific publications and local nature magazines.  Members of the MLSS Board of Directors have given presentations to several local nature clubs, federal government and municipal government staff meetings.

World Wildlife Fund Canada (WWF-Canada) is a national registered charity formed for the conservation of biodiversity in Canada and elsewhere. In the 2020 fiscal year, WWF-Canada's public policy dialogue and development activities (PPDDAs) were aimed at the creation of, or changes to public policy that will contribute to the long-term protection and sustainable management of ecosystems and healthy species populations on land, and in freshwater and marine environments. These PPDDAs involved: the conduct and public dissemination of research about the benefits of public policy to species and ecosystems; sharing, both publicly and directly with government, well-researched and evidence-based information about public policy needs; public advocacy campaigns aimed to garner support for public policy changes and decisions; and making non-partisan representations to elected and public officials, parliamentary committees, and candidates and political parties about public policies that will promote the long-term health of species and ecosystems.
